boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Portland
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food destinations with current, source-listed late availability in North Portland or elsewhere in Portland.

cards.title: Taco Bell on N Lombard
cards.subtitle: 4909 N Lombard St, Portland
cards.notes: Use the N Lombard drive-thru when you need a food stop after evening plans; confirm holiday changes before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A North Portland drive-thru listed through 3 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official location page lists its 4909 N Lombard St drive-thru as open until 3:00 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru hours of 3:00 a.m. daily; dine-in hours are earlier. Holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Taco Bell on N Interstate
cards.subtitle: 4616 N Interstate Ave, Portland
cards.notes: Choose this N Interstate location for a late drive-thru food option, and check the location page again if visiting on a holiday.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Taco Bell location listed open until 4 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official Portland location directory lists the 4616 N Interstate Ave restaurant as open until 4:00 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official directory lists this location as open until 4:00 a.m.; verify service mode and holiday changes with the restaurant.

cards.title: Taco Bell at Jantzen Beach
cards.subtitle: 12237 N Jantzen Dr, Portland
cards.notes: If you are already headed toward Jantzen Beach, this is a late drive-thru option; review the location page before departure.
cards.short_summary: A Jantzen Beach Taco Bell listed open until 3 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official Portland location directory lists 12237 N Jantzen Dr as open until 3:00 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official directory lists this location as open until 3:00 a.m.; confirm current drive-thru availability and holiday hours.

cards.title: Domino's at 4908 N Lombard
cards.subtitle: 4908 N Lombard St, Portland
cards.notes: Place a carryout or delivery order from the North Lombard store when its posted midnight closing fits your evening schedule.
cards.short_summary: A North Lombard pizza location currently shown open until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s official page for 4908 N Lombard St identifies the Portland store and shows it open until 12:00 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official store page currently displays “Open Today Until 12:00 AM”; Domino’s says store hours vary by location.

cards.title: Domino's at 8040 N Lombard
cards.subtitle: 8040 N Lombard St, Portland
cards.notes: Use the farther-west Lombard store as a carryout or delivery option, checking the store’s live hours before you order.
cards.short_summary: A second North Lombard pizza stop with location-specific hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s official page identifies its 8040 N Lombard St Portland store and directs visitors to its Hours section for current store hours.
cards.access_notes: Official page identifies the 8040 N Lombard store and states that location hours vary; it currently lists the store among locations open until midnight.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on N Lombard
cards.subtitle: 5265 N Lombard St, Portland
cards.notes: Order carryout or delivery from this N Lombard location when the posted 1 a.m. schedule works; check for changes first.
cards.short_summary: A N Lombard pizza stop with 1 a.m. hours listed every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut’s official page lists both delivery and carryout at 5265 N Lombard St from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 a.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists delivery and carryout through 1:00 a.m. daily, while noting that delivery hours may vary.

cards.title: Wendy's on N Lombard
cards.subtitle: 1405 N Lombard, Portland
cards.notes: Keep this N Lombard restaurant in mind for an evening food stop; its official schedule lists both restaurant and drive-thru service to midnight.
cards.short_summary: A North Lombard restaurant and drive-thru open until midnight daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s official location page lists restaurant and drive-thru hours at 1405 N Lombard as 6:30 a.m.–12:00 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant and drive-thru service through 12:00 a.m. daily; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Fino in Kenton
cards.subtitle: 8225 N Denver Ave, Portland
cards.notes: Plan a Friday or Saturday dinner in Kenton when a later sit-down meal fits; call ahead or use the official takeout link.
cards.short_summary: A Kenton pasta-and-pizza restaurant with 10 p.m. weekend dinner hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Fino’s official site lists dinner until 10:00 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays at 8225 N Denver Ave.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday–Saturday dinner from 4:00–10:00 p.m.; Sunday–Thursday dinner ends at 9:00 p.m.

cards.title: Janken in the Pearl District
cards.subtitle: 250 NW 13th Ave, Portland
cards.notes: For a later Portland dinner, reserve or confirm service directly with Janken before making the trip from campus.
cards.short_summary: A Pearl District restaurant whose official hours run to 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Janken’s official site lists hours until 11:00 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays at 250 NW 13th Ave.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday and Saturday hours of 5:00–11:00 p.m.; Tuesday–Thursday and Sunday service ends at 10:00 p.m.

cards.title: Xport Rooftop Lounge
cards.subtitle: 1355 SW 2nd Ave, Portland
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s current service policy and make a reservation if needed before planning a late dinner in downtown Portland.
cards.short_summary: A downtown restaurant location whose official page lists 11 p.m. closing daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Xport’s official contact page lists its 1355 SW 2nd Ave Portland location open from 5:00–11:00 p.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official contact page lists hours of 5:00–11:00 p.m. Monday through Sunday; reservations are available through the site.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named University of Portland spaces for studying, gathering, reflection, recreation, and campus events.

cards.title: Settle into Franz Lounge
cards.subtitle: Dundon-Berchtold Hall
cards.notes: Bring a reading or laptop to the lounge’s armchairs and tables, then move to another common area if a scheduled event needs the room.
cards.short_summary: A furnished Dundon-Berchtold Hall lounge suited to individual work between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland identifies Franz Lounge in Dundon-Berchtold Hall as a spacious study option with settees, coffee tables, and armchairs.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Dundon-Berchtold Hall; follow posted room-use guidance.

cards.title: Use Clark Library’s study choices
cards.subtitle: Clark Library
cards.notes: Choose the seating that fits your task, or reserve a group room, booth, or individual carrel through the library’s current process.
cards.short_summary: The campus library combines quiet seating with reservable study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland says Clark Library offers quiet study, seating and outlets, plus reservable group study rooms, booths, and individual carrels.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Library spaces and room reservations may have current eligibility or booking rules.

cards.title: Work by the Vollum Study Room windows
cards.subtitle: Shiley Hall
cards.notes: Use a desk or reference shelf in this two-floor study space, and keep the room ready for others by packing out your materials when finished.
cards.short_summary: A two-level School of Engineering study room with desks, reference materials, and windows.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland describes the Vollum Study Room in Shiley Hall as a two-floor space with desks, reference materials, and a wall of windows.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Shiley Hall; observe any school or room-use notices.

cards.title: Read on the Quiet Side
cards.subtitle: Bauccio Commons
cards.notes: Use the quieter side for a meal-and-reading break when it is not reserved, and plan ahead if you need a wall outlet for longer work.
cards.short_summary: A designated quieter side of the campus commons that can support study alongside dining.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland identifies the Quiet Side of Bauccio Commons as a study option when it is not otherwise in use.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Use only when not otherwise in use; dining purchases may be required for food.

cards.title: Pause in Holy Cross Lounge
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Franz Hall
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for a quiet reading session; use the available seating and outlets considerately, especially during busy class periods.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor Franz Hall lounge with banquette seating and a quiet atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland places Holy Cross Lounge on the third floor of Franz Hall and describes it as quiet and peaceful, with seating and outlets.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located across from the Garaventa Center entrance in Franz Hall.

cards.title: Meet up in St. Mary’s Lounge
cards.subtitle: St. Mary’s Student Center
cards.notes: Choose this lounge for collaborative work or a casual meet-up, and shift to a quieter setting if you need uninterrupted concentration.
cards.short_summary: A lounge in the student center described by the University as an active hangout space.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland describes the St. Mary’s lounge as a college hangout space where activity is commonly taking place.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in St. Mary’s Student Center; access may vary with student-center programming.

cards.title: Move between study sessions
cards.subtitle: Beauchamp Recreation & Wellness Center
cards.notes: Bring appropriate workout gear, check current recreation policies, and choose a court, track, climbing, fitness, or equipment activity that fits your plan.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation facility supporting exercise, climbing, basketball, bike rentals, and more.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland lists basketball, weights, bike rentals, climbing, and other activities at the Beauchamp Recreation and Wellness Center.
cards.access_notes: Recreation access and equipment use are subject to current Recreational Services policies.

cards.title: Join a garden activity at S.L.U.G.
cards.subtitle: Student Led Unity Garden, 6615 N. McKenna Ave.
cards.notes: Watch for registered garden programs, then join hands-on planting or activities with the organizers’ directions and the site’s weather-ready guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named campus garden used for hands-on planting and community activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UP Biology describes the Student Led Unity Garden as the site of a University of Portland hands-on gardening and community event.
cards.access_notes: Event participation may require advance registration and is subject to organizer instructions.

cards.title: Attend Mass or take a reflective pause
cards.subtitle: Chapel of Christ the Teacher
cards.notes: Check Campus Ministry’s current schedule before attending Mass or other programs, and use the space respectfully around services and individual reflection.
cards.short_summary: The University chapel hosts Mass and is central to Campus Ministry programming.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland’s 2025–26 viewbook states that students may attend Mass in the Chapel of Christ the Teacher and join Campus Ministry programs.
cards.access_notes: Religious services and programs follow Campus Ministry’s current schedule.

cards.title: Look for an exhibit in Buckley
cards.subtitle: First floor, Buckley Center
cards.notes: Check the University calendar for the current exhibition or reception, then visit during its listed access window and follow any gallery instructions.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Buckley Center gallery used for University exhibition programming.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland’s event calendar identifies the Buckley Center Art Gallery on the first floor as a venue for an art exhibit and reception.
cards.source_title: Buckley Center | University of Portland Events Calendar
cards.access_notes: Exhibition availability depends on the University’s current calendar and gallery schedule.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-purchase outdoor and public-program options near the University of Portland, using City of Portland access information and University-hosted free-event listings.

cards.title: Walk the Cathedral Park Nature Patch
cards.subtitle: Cathedral Park, St. Johns
cards.notes: Meet beneath the St. Johns Bridge and take the gravel-and-path loop through the garden spaces; keep the plan to walking and looking, with no reservation needed.
cards.short_summary: A planted walk beneath the bridge with paths, picnic nooks, and river-adjacent views.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks identifies the Nature Patch as garden spaces with a gravel pathway and says Cathedral Park is open 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Use the park during its posted 5 a.m.–midnight hours. The boat-ramp lot has a fee; arrive on foot, bike, transit, or use another legal option.

cards.title: Bring a no-purchase picnic-table hang
cards.subtitle: Cathedral Park, St. Johns
cards.notes: Pick an unreserved table, bring water or something from home, and leave the spot ready for the next group; a reservation is only for guaranteed use.
cards.short_summary: A first-come outdoor table hang under the bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: The park lists picnic tables, and Portland Parks says individual picnic tables are available first-come, first-served; reservations are for guaranteed use.
cards.access_notes: Choose an individual, unreserved table. A permit is required for a guaranteed site, equipment setup, alcohol, advertising, or large gatherings.

cards.title: Follow the paths at Columbia Park Nature Patch
cards.subtitle: Columbia Park and Annex, North Portland
cards.notes: Walk the nature patch’s path network and pause at the log benches or boulders; this works well as a low-key conversation stop without bringing equipment.
cards.short_summary: A compact garden walk among trees, planted areas, and informal seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks describes Columbia Park Nature Patch as having log benches, boulders, walking paths, and pollinator-focused plantings; park hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.source_title: Columbia Park and Annex | Portland Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Visit during posted park hours. Stay on established paths and observe posted closures or field reservations.

cards.title: Use an unreserved Columbia Park table
cards.subtitle: Columbia Park and Annex, North Portland
cards.notes: Claim one available individual table for a chat or study break; if a group needs a guaranteed site, check the City’s reservation rules instead of assuming it is open.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, first-come table meet-up in a 35-acre city park.
cards.evidence_claim: Columbia Park lists picnic tables, while Portland Parks states individual picnic tables in many parks are available first-come, first-served.
cards.access_notes: No reservation is needed for an available individual table; permits apply when a group needs guaranteed use or meets listed permit conditions.

cards.title: Shoot around at McKenna Park
cards.subtitle: McKenna Park, University Park neighborhood
cards.notes: Bring a ball from home and use the outdoor court for a casual shoot-around; yield to others and avoid treating any field or court as reserved unless posted.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor basketball-court stop near UP’s University Park neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks lists a basketball court at McKenna Park and says the resurfaced court is complete and ready for play; park hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Bring your own ball. The City directs visitors to reserve a sports field only when they need a reservation.

cards.title: Take a loop on McKenna’s paved paths
cards.subtitle: McKenna Park, University Park neighborhood
cards.notes: Use the paved paths for an easy walking-and-talking loop, then leave space around active games and playground users; plan around the City’s posted park hours.
cards.short_summary: A simple no-equipment walking loop close to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: McKenna Park’s City listing includes paved paths and gives park hours of 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: No equipment or reservation is needed for walking; observe any temporary closures and leash rules.

cards.title: Walk the open lawn and paths at University Park
cards.subtitle: University Park, Portsmouth
cards.notes: Meet at the park entrance on N Foss Avenue and make a relaxed lap on the paved paths; the open lawn gives a straightforward place to sit and talk.
cards.short_summary: A nearby 11-acre municipal park with paths and open lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks describes University Park as having mature trees, open lawn areas, a playground, and park paths; its posted hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.source_title: North Portland Parks Improvement Projects | Portland Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Use the park during posted hours and avoid organized-field activity. No purchase or admission is listed for walking the public park.

cards.title: Walk Portsmouth Park together
cards.subtitle: Portsmouth Park, North Portland
cards.notes: Use the public park for a short walking-and-chat break, keeping clear of scheduled field use and leaving pets leashed; no special gear is needed for the walk.
cards.short_summary: A compact neighborhood-park walk with open sports fields.
cards.evidence_claim: Portsmouth Park is a City park with soccer and softball fields and posted hours of 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Walking does not require a reservation; the City advises reserving a sports field when a group needs one.

cards.title: Take a shaded walk at Pier Park
cards.subtitle: Pier Park, St. Johns
cards.notes: Choose the park’s shaded trails for a longer walk with a friend; keep to paths, share space with other visitors, and skip the pool or rentals for a no-purchase visit.
cards.short_summary: A forested 85-acre park walk in North Portland.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks describes Pier Park’s shaded trails and lists paved and unpaved paths; park hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Use trails during park hours. This card excludes the pool and reservable picnic site; a walk requires no purchase or admission.

cards.entity_name: University Park Neighborhood Association general meeting
cards.title: Attend a University Park neighborhood meeting
cards.subtitle: Chiles Center, University of Portland
cards.notes: Check the association’s listing before going, then attend to hear neighborhood discussion and meet local residents; the City states that everyone is welcome.
cards.short_summary: A public neighborhood conversation hosted at UP’s Chiles Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Portland says University Park Neighborhood Association general meetings are held at UP’s Chiles Center, are open to the public, and welcome everyone.
cards.source_title: University Park neighborhood | City of Portland
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current date, location, and format with the association before attending; the City’s listing says general meetings are open to the public.

warnings: For park cards, cost-free status covers the listed walking, table, and casual-use activity only; reservable sites, sports fields, parking, pools, and equipment can have separate rules or costs.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named University of Portland study settings, selected for documented seating, quiet-space, or project-work features.

cards.title: Franz Lounge
cards.subtitle: Dundon-Berchtold Hall
cards.notes: Set up with a reading or writing task at a coffee table or armchair; the university describes the lounge as having settees, coffee tables, and armchairs.
cards.short_summary: A furnished lounge setting inside Dundon-Berchtold Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland identifies Franz Lounge as a study location with settees, coffee tables, and armchairs.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Dundon-Berchtold Hall; confirm building access and room availability on arrival.

cards.title: First-Floor Hallway Seating
cards.subtitle: Dundon-Berchtold Hall
cards.notes: Use the desk-and-chair stations for focused work, or choose couch and armchair seating; wall outlets support device charging.
cards.short_summary: Hallway seating with desks, soft seating, outlets, and lawn-facing windows.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland describes first-floor hallway study areas with desks, chairs, couches, armchairs, wall outlets, and windows onto the lawn.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Inside Dundon-Berchtold Hall; use open seating and avoid blocking hallway circulation.

cards.title: Second-Floor Hallway Seating
cards.subtitle: Dundon-Berchtold Hall
cards.notes: Bring a charged laptop and pick between desk seating and couches by the lawn-facing windows; use wall outlets when available.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor open study area with mixed seating and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland lists the second-floor hallways as study spaces with desks, chairs, couches, armchairs, outlets, and lawn-facing windows.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Inside Dundon-Berchtold Hall; availability varies with classes and events.

cards.title: Basement Hallway Study Area
cards.subtitle: Dundon-Berchtold Hall
cards.notes: Choose a desk set or couch seating for a distraction-light session; the university notes this floor has the same seating types as other study hallways.
cards.short_summary: A basement-level hallway option with desks and soft seating.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland describes the Dundon-Berchtold basement hallway as a low-traffic study area with desk sets plus couch seating.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Inside Dundon-Berchtold Hall; check that the hallway remains open for academic use.

cards.title: Clark Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Clark Library
cards.notes: Reserve a group room when a project needs a contained workspace; the university lists 20 reservable group study rooms in Clark Library.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms for collaborative study in the campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland states that Clark Library has 20 reservable group study rooms.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; use the library’s current room-reservation system for availability and eligibility.

cards.title: Clark Library Study Booths
cards.subtitle: Clark Library
cards.notes: Reserve a booth for a compact work session or pair meeting; the university identifies five reservable study booths in the library.
cards.short_summary: Five reservable booths within Clark Library.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland states that Clark Library offers five reservable study booths.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; consult the library’s current booking system before going.

cards.title: Clark Library Individual Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Clark Library
cards.notes: Reserve an individual carrel when you need a defined solo workstation; the university lists 12 individual study carrels among library reservations.
cards.short_summary: Twelve reservable individual workstations in Clark Library.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland states that Clark Library has 12 individual study carrels available as reservable spots.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; check the library’s current booking system and applicable access rules.

cards.title: Vollum Study Room
cards.subtitle: Shiley Hall
cards.notes: Use the two-floor room for desk work or reference consultation; its wall of windows provides natural light across the space.
cards.short_summary: A two-level engineering study room with desks, reference materials, and windows.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland describes the Vollum Study Room as a two-floor space with desks, reference shelves, and a wall of windows.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Shiley Hall; check building access and room conditions before settling in.

cards.title: Quiet Side of Bauccio Commons
cards.subtitle: Bauccio Commons
cards.notes: Bring reading or laptop work to the quieter side of the Commons when it is not in use; wall-adjacent tables offer the documented outlet access.
cards.short_summary: A dining-building study setting with limited wall-outlet seating.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland identifies the Quiet Side of Bauccio Commons as a study option when it is not otherwise in use, noting outlets are by walls.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Use only when the area is not otherwise in use; food purchase is not required by this listing, but is not independently verified.

cards.title: Holy Cross Lounge
cards.subtitle: Third Floor, Franz Hall
cards.notes: Work at the wall banquette seating and use an outlet if available; the lounge is across from the Garaventa Center entrance on Franz Hall’s third floor.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor Franz Hall lounge with banquette seating and historical portraits.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland locates Holy Cross Lounge on Franz Hall’s third floor and describes banquette seating, outlets, and portraits of past UP presidents.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Across from the Garaventa Center entrance; confirm lounge availability around scheduled campus activity.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named North Portland destinations, each anchored to a nearby corridor and a specific documented activity or feature.

cards.title: University Park — lighted ball field
cards.subtitle: N Foss Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the paved paths and use the picnic tables; the city identifies this as its only baseball and softball field with lights outside Delta Park.
cards.short_summary: A nearby park with fields, paths, and picnic tables.
cards.evidence_claim: University Park includes playgrounds, paved paths, picnic tables, and Portland Parks’ only baseball and softball field with lights outside Delta Park.
cards.access_notes: City park; observe posted rules and field-use guidance.

cards.title: Columbia Park — nature-patch paths
cards.subtitle: N Lombard Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter at Lombard and Woolsey, then follow the walking paths through the nature patch with its planted lawn, log benches, and boulders.
cards.short_summary: A 35-acre park with a documented nature patch.
cards.evidence_claim: Columbia Park and Annex has walking paths, a nature patch, sports fields, a historic cottage, and the annex directly across N Lombard Street.
cards.access_notes: Park hours listed by the city are 5:00am–midnight.

cards.title: Pier Park — choose a court or trail
cards.subtitle: N Lombard Street corridor
cards.notes: Start from the Lombard and Bruce entrance and choose among the paved and unpaved paths, sports courts, picnic areas, or the skate park.
cards.short_summary: An 85-acre city park with varied outdoor amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Pier Park has trails, picnic areas, a skate park, courts, sports fields, a splash pad, and a disc golf course.
cards.access_notes: Park hours listed by the city are 5:00am–midnight; dogs must be leashed.

cards.title: Cathedral Park — bridge-side paths
cards.subtitle: N Edison Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the paved paths and picnic areas beneath St. Johns Bridge, and look for the nature patch’s flowering gardens, log features, and basalt elements.
cards.short_summary: A riverfront park directly beneath St. Johns Bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: Cathedral Park offers paved paths, picnic tables, riverfront views, a stage, and a nature patch under St. Johns Bridge.
cards.access_notes: Park hours listed by the city are 5:00am–midnight; use designated paths and areas.

cards.title: St. Johns Library — computers and Wi‑Fi
cards.subtitle: N Charleston Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Set up a focused work stop using the library’s computers, Wi‑Fi, scanner, printers, and laptop-lending kiosk; verify the day’s hours before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A public library branch with study-supporting services.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Johns Library provides computers, Wi‑Fi, scanning, printing, and a laptop-lending kiosk at 7510 N Charleston Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Current listed hours vary by day; confirm on the library’s location page.

cards.title: St. Johns Twin Cinemas — current films
cards.subtitle: N Lombard Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the cinema’s current program before heading to 8704 N Lombard; it identifies itself as a first-run cinema, so showtimes determine the visit.
cards.short_summary: A named N Lombard venue for scheduled film screenings.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Johns Twin Cinemas is a first-run cinema located at 8704 N Lombard Street.
cards.access_notes: Check the official cinema site for current films and showtimes.

cards.title: Portsmouth Park — field time
cards.subtitle: N Stanford Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Meet at Stanford and Depauw for the playground, soccer field, or softball field, and keep plans within the city’s posted park hours.
cards.short_summary: A compact Portsmouth park with play and field space.
cards.evidence_claim: Portsmouth Park has a playground, soccer field, and softball field at N Stanford Avenue and Depauw Street.
cards.access_notes: Park hours listed by the city are 5:00am–midnight; dogs must be leashed.

cards.title: St. Johns Park — community-center stop
cards.subtitle: N Central Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the N Central Street address as a meeting point, then pair outdoor time in the park with a visit to the St. Johns Community Center on site.
cards.short_summary: A city park that contains the St. Johns Community Center.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Johns Park contains the St. Johns Community Center and is located in the St. Johns community.
cards.access_notes: Check Portland Parks for current community-center programming and park information.

cards.title: Peninsula Crossing Trail — bike or hike
cards.subtitle: N Willamette Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Use the N Willamette Boulevard end for a bike or hike outing; the city lists the route to Columbia Boulevard and identifies both trail activities.
cards.short_summary: A named North Portland trail spanning two major corridors.
cards.evidence_claim: Peninsula Crossing Trail runs from N Willamette Boulevard to Columbia Boulevard and supports biking and hiking.
cards.access_notes: Check the city’s trail closures and delays information before traveling.

cards.title: George Park — N Fessenden play space
cards.subtitle: N Fessenden Street corridor
cards.notes: Find the park between Calhoun and Burr for its playground, walking path, picnic table, and lawn; check the city project page for current work status.
cards.short_summary: A St. Johns park with a documented redevelopment project.
cards.evidence_claim: George Park is along N Fessenden Street between N Calhoun and N Burr and includes a playground, walking path, picnic table, and open lawn.
cards.access_notes: The city lists an active redevelopment project; consult its page for current conditions.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented University of Portland rituals, recurring campus celebrations, and Pilot-specific practices.

cards.title: Light a candle at the Bell Tower Ceremony
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation • Academic Quad
cards.notes: During orientation, join the candlelit gathering in the Academic Quad and listen to the Bell Tower music marking the start of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A candlelit orientation ritual beneath UP’s Bell Tower.
